subtitle: When the Deccan Stallion Smelt the Ganga Winds

panels.action: Govinda III sits astride a powerful warhorse on a dusty northern plain, cloak and hair stirred by wind, distant hints of the Ganga valley and the hazy silhouette of Kanauj on the horizon.

dialogue.text: Govinda III of the Rashtrakutas rides from the Deccan toward Kanauj, into the storm of the Tripartite Struggle.

i18n.hi: राश्ट्रकूट गोविन्द तृतीय दक्खिन से कन्नौज की ओर, त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष के तूफ़ान में सवार हुआ।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot from elevated angle
panels.action: A grand view of Manyakheta: tiled roofs, temple spires and busy markets, with Govinda III standing on a palace terrace, overlooking the city and the distant, hazy line of the northern horizon.

dialogue.text: From Manyakheta in the Deccan, the Rashtrakutas watched the north. Beyond forests and rivers lay Kanauj, throne of old emperors, prize of a new age.

i18n.hi: दक्खिन के मानीयखेता से राश्ट्रकूट उत्तर को निहारते थे। जंगलों–नदियों के पार था कन्नौज, पुराने सम्राटों का सिंहासन, नए समय का इनाम।

panels.action: Govinda III, in early middle age, stands in a pillared hall, hand resting on the hilt of his sword, face calm but intent, as a courtier gestures toward a painted map of northern India on a cloth.

dialogue.text: By c. 800, three powers circled Kanauj. The Palas from the east, the Gurjara-Pratiharas from the west, and now the Rashtrakuta horse from the south.

i18n.hi: लगभग 800 तक, तीन ताकतें कन्नौज के चारों ओर मंडरा रही थीं। पूरब से पाल, पश्चिम से गुर्जर–प्रतिहार, और अब दक्षिण से राश्ट्रकूट अश्व।

panels.action: Over Govinda III’s shoulder we see a court scholar pointing at Kanauj on a stylized map, the river Ganga painted in blue, while tiny markers show rival banners pressing toward the city from three directions.

dialogue.text: Kanauj was more than a city. It was a word that meant overlordship, a seat sung in prashastis, where one king’s name tried to rise above all others.

i18n.hi: कन्नौज सिर्फ़ शहर नहीं था। वो एक नाम था, अधिपति का अर्थ, प्रशस्तियों में गाया सिंहासन, जहाँ एक राजा का नाम सब पर चढ़ना चाहता था।

panels.action: Close on Govinda III’s face as he listens, lamplight catching in his eyes; behind him, a faint relief carving of his father Dhruva reminds us of an earlier generation’s northern ride.

dialogue.text: Govinda’s father, Dhruva, had once ridden north. Now the son weighed a new march, careful not to confuse old glory with present chance.

i18n.hi: गोविन्द के पिता ध्रुवा कभी उत्तर को दौड़े थे। अब बेटा नई चढ़ाई तौल रहा था, कि पुरानी शान आज की बाज़ी न बना बैठे।

panels.action: A bird’s-eye view of a vast Rashtrakuta camp outside Manyakheta: rows of tents, cavalry lines, elephants being fed, standards with the royal emblem fluttering, while Govinda III rides along the ranks inspecting them.

dialogue.text: He gathered his strength. Deccan horsemen, elephant corps, archers hardened by southern wars, all called to follow their king toward the Ganga plains.

i18n.hi: उसने बल जुटाया। दक्खिन के घुड़सवार, गज दल, दक्षिणी युद्धों से कड़े धनुर्धर, सबको गंगा के मैदानों की ओर अपने राजा के पीछे बुलाया।

panels.shot: dynamic tracking shot at horse level
panels.action: Govinda III gallops at the head of his cavalry, hooves kicking up dust as the column snakes through a rocky Deccan pass toward greener northern lands.

dialogue.text: Inscribed later on copper, his scribes would boast that the earth trembled under his march. Between rock and sky, only hoofbeats answered them.

i18n.hi: बाद में ताँबे पर लिखकर, उसके लेखकों ने शेखी मारी कि उसके मार्च से धरती काँपी। पत्थर और आसमान के बीच बस टापें ही गूँजीं।

panels.action: The army fords a broad river under a grey sky; Govinda III rides onto a crude wooden ferry for his elephant, watching the far bank where northern villages and fields begin.

dialogue.text: One by one, the southern ridges fell behind. Rivers were crossed, forests thinned, and the air grew heavier with the damp breath of the Ganga lands.

i18n.hi: एक–एक करके दक्षिणी पहाड़ियाँ पीछे छूट गईं। नदियाँ पार हुईं, जंगल छँटे, और हवा गंगा भूमि की नम साँस से भारी होती गई।

panels.action: In a northern village street, peasants and traders look on warily as Rashtrakuta soldiers march past; Govinda III pauses to speak with a grey-bearded local headman who gestures eastward and westward, torn between fears.

dialogue.text: Between Pala and Pratihara claims, local chiefs had long bent and straightened. Now a third banner filled their lanes with dust.

i18n.hi: पाल–प्रतिहार दावों के बीच, स्थानीय मुखिया कभी झुकते, कभी सीध होते रहे थे। अब तीसरा ध्वज उनकी राहों में धूल भरता आया।

panels.action: On a flat plain, two distant forces face each other: Rashtrakuta lines on one side, a northern host with elephants and bannered chariots on the other, the two armies still at wary distance as scouts ride between.

dialogue.text: The copper plates would later speak of many kings subdued. In truth, each field was a negotiation of steel, fatigue and fear between men who knew the north was no one’s forever.

i18n.hi: ताँबे की पट्टिकाएँ बाद में कई राजाओं के दबने की बातें करेंगी। असल में हर खेत लोहे, थकान और डर की बातचीत थी, उन लोगों के बीच जो जानते थे कि उत्तर किसी का हमेशा नहीं।

panels.action: Govinda III sits in a campaign pavilion, armour loosened, as a northern envoy kneels, offering a tray with a royal seal and gifts; Rashtrakuta officers stand behind, gauging the envoy’s calm eyes.

dialogue.text: Some rulers fought. Others sent gifts and seals of submission, hoping the southern wave would pass quickly, leaving their thrones standing in the receding foam.

i18n.hi: कुछ शासक लड़े। कुछ ने भेंट और आत्मसमर्पण की मुद्राएँ भेजीं, कि दक्षिणी लहर जल्दी उतर जाए, और उनका सिंहासन झाग के पीछे भी खड़ा रहे।

panels.action: From a low hill, Govinda III and his captains look toward Kanauj in the distance: ramparts and towers shimmer in the heat, Ganga branches glinting below, smoke of many hearths rising.

dialogue.text: At last Kanauj lay before him, not as a conquered corpse, but as a living city, wary and watching, its fame larger than its walls.

i18n.hi: आख़िर कन्नौज सामने था, जीता हुआ मुर्दा नहीं, जिंदा शहर, चौकन्ना, देखता हुआ, जिसका नाम उसकी दीवारों से बड़ा था।

panels.shot: tight shot on banner against skyline
panels.action: A Rashtrakuta banner is planted on a rise facing Kanauj, its cloth snapping against a bright sky, the city’s skyline blurred in the background, soldiers arrayed in disciplined lines below.

dialogue.text: Radhanpur’s plates would later claim that kings of Kanauj bowed and the Ganga drank his horse’s reflection. Such words were armour hammered from ink and pride.

i18n.hi: राधनपुर की पट्टिकाएँ लिखेंगी कि कन्नौज के राजा झुके और गंगा ने उसके घोड़े का प्रतिबिंब पिया। ऐसे शब्द स्याही और अभिमान से गढ़ी हुई कवच थे।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in Kanauj court
panels.action: Inside a northern hall, a local ruler or governor confers with his counsellors, glancing toward an open window through which Rashtrakuta standards are just visible on the outskirts, faces tense as they weigh resistance and submission.

dialogue.text: Within Kanauj and her satellite courts, talk shifted. For a while, Rashtrakuta might be written as overlord, even as Pratihara and Pala scribes sharpened their own stories.

i18n.hi: कन्नौज और उसके उपदालों की अदालतों में बात बदली। कुछ समय के लिए राश्ट्रकूट को अधिपति लिखा जा सकता था, जब कि प्रतिहार और पाल लेखक अपनी कथाएँ तेज कर रहे थे।

panels.shot: close-up on copper plate being inscribed
panels.action: A royal scribe crouches over a gleaming copper plate, careful hands incising Nagari characters, while Govinda III sits in the background listening as a court poet recites a freshly composed eulogy.

dialogue.text: In the south, scribes recorded the tale. The Radhanpur plates speak of humbled north and bent skies, their verses as much wish as memory.

i18n.hi: दक्खिन में लिपिकार कथा दर्ज कर रहे थे। राधनपुर की पट्टिकाएँ झुके हुए उत्तर और झुके आसमान की कहानियाँ कहती हैं, जिनके छंद उतनी चाहत हैं जितनी याद।

panels.shot: wide shot of army beginning return march
panels.action: The Rashtrakuta army begins its southward turn from the Ganga plains, long columns stretching across a landscape of harvested fields, Govinda III glancing back once toward the fading outline of Kanauj.

dialogue.text: Yet the Deccan could not stay in the north. The campaign ended, the horse turned homeward, leaving behind not garrisons and land-rolls, but impressions and fears.

i18n.hi: पर दक्खिन उत्तर में टिक नहीं सकता था। अभियान ख़त्म हुआ, अश्व पलट चला, पीछे चौकियाँ–जागीरें नहीं, छापें और डर छोड़कर।

panels.action: A split composition: on one side, Govinda III seated in Manyakheta’s durbar receiving northern envoys; on the other, a Pratihara king in Gwalior and a Pala king near the Badal pillar each presides over their own courts, scribes writing prashastis.

dialogue.text: Pratihara and Pala stones tell rival glories. Cross-read, they reveal not one conqueror, but a long jostling of prestige in which each king claimed, and re-claimed, Kanauj.

i18n.hi: प्रतिहार और पाल के पत्थर अपनी–अपनी महिमा गाते हैं। साथ पढ़ो, तो एक विजेता नहीं, नाम के धक्के–मुक्के दिखते हैं, जिसमें हर राजा कन्नौज को पाता और फिर से पाता है।

panels.shot: medium shot in quiet palace chamber
panels.action: Govinda III sits quietly in a palace chamber, armour set aside, examining a northern coin and a small model of Kanauj on a tray, a faint, thoughtful smile on his face as lamplight flickers.

dialogue.speaker: govinda_iii
dialogue.text: Some thrones are better chased than chained.

i18n.hi: कुछ सिंहासन बाँधने से ज़्यादा, दौड़ने में चमकते हैं।

panels.shot: wide closing shot of Deccan landscape
panels.action: The sun sets over the Deccan plains around Manyakheta; distant Rashtrakuta standards flutter on ramparts as traders and travellers move along a road, hinting at the wide world that knew Govinda III’s name.

dialogue.text: Govinda III returned with fame that reached the Ganga, not rule that held it. His ride toward Kanauj showed how prestige can dazzle from afar, yet slip like river fog when grasped.

i18n.hi: गोविन्द तृतीय लौटा ऐसी कीर्ति के साथ जो गंगा तक पहुँची, पर ऐसा राज नहीं जो उसे थाम ले। उसका कन्नौज की ओर सवार होना दिखा गया कि यश दूर से चमकता है, पर पकड़ो तो नदी के कुहरे सा हाथ से फिसल जाता है।

title_i18n.hi: गोविन्द तृतीय कन्नौज की ओर दौड़ता है

subtitle_i18n.en: When the Deccan Stallion Smelt the Ganga Winds
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब दक्खिनी अश्व ने गंगा की हवा सूंघी
